title: Right pyramids, right cones and spheres

sections.title: Right pyramids, right cones and spheres

subtopics.title: Surface area of pyramids
subtopics.exposition: A pyramid is a geometric solid that has a polygon as its base and faces that converge at a point called the apex. In a pyramid the faces are not perpendicular to the base. A pyramid is called a right pyramid if the line between the apex and the centre of the base is perpendicular to the base. The surface area of a square pyramid is the area of the base plus the area of the triangular sides. For a square pyramid, surface area = b² + 4(½ b h_s), where b² is the area of the base and each of the 4 triangular sides has area ½ b h_s. The surface area of a square pyramid simplifies to b(b + 2h_s). The surface area of a triangular pyramid is the area of the base plus the area of the triangular sides. For a triangular pyramid, surface area = (½ b × h_b) + 3(½ b × h_s), where (½ b × h_b) is the area of the triangular base and 3(½ b × h_s) is the area of the three triangular sides. The surface area of a triangular pyramid simplifies to ½ b (h_b + 3h_s). To find the surface area of a triangular pyramid, first find the area of the base triangle using area = ½ b h_b. The height of the base triangle (h_b) is found using the theorem of Pythagoras. The area of the three triangular sides of the triangular pyramid is 3(½ × b × h_s); in the worked example, 3(½ × 6 × 10) = 90 cm². Add the area of the base and the area of the sides to get the surface area of the triangular pyramid; in the worked example 9√3 + 90 = 105.6 cm². The triangular pyramid and the square pyramid take their names from the shape of their base. The surface area of the triangular pyramid is asked for correct to one decimal place. The surface area of the triangular pyramid is given in square centimetres (cm²).

subtopics.title: Surface area of a cone
subtopics.exposition: Cones are similar to pyramids except that their bases are circles instead of polygons. A cone has two faces: the base and the walls. The base is a circle of radius r. The surface area of a right cone is the area of the base plus the area of the walls. For a right cone, surface area = πr² + ½ × 2πrh, where πr² is the area of the circular base and ½ × 2πrh is the area of the walls. The surface area of a right cone simplifies to πr(r + h). A cone with height h and base of radius r has surface area πr² + πr√(r² + h²). The surface area of a cone with height h and base radius r can be written as πr(r + √(r² + h²)). To find the surface area of a cone, first find the area of the circular base using area = πr²; in the worked example with r = 4 this is π × 4² = 16π. The area of the walls (sides) of the cone is πrh, where h is the slant height. The slant height of the cone is found using the theorem of Pythagoras. Add the area of the base and the area of the walls to get the total surface area of the cone; in the worked example 16π + 8π√53 = 233.2 cm². The walls of a cone can be opened out to a sector of a circle. The curved surface can be cut into many thin triangles with height close to a, the slant height, and the areas of these triangles are summed. The area of the sector is ½ × base × height (of a small triangle). Taking the base as 2πr and the height as a, the area of the sector is ½ × 2πr × a = πra. The slant height a is calculated using the theorem of Pythagoras: a = √(r² + h²). The area of the circular base is A_b = πr². The area of the curved walls is A_w = πra = πr√(r² + h²). The surface area A of the cone is the sum of the areas, A = A_b + A_w = πr² + πr√(r² + h²). In the formula for the area of the walls πrh, the letter h stands for the slant height of the cone. The surface area of the cone is asked for correct to 1 decimal place. When deriving the cone's surface area, the cone has height h and base radius r, and a denotes the slant height.

subtopics.title: Surface area of a sphere
subtopics.exposition: Spheres are solids that are perfectly round and look the same from any direction. The surface area of a sphere is 4πr², where r is the radius. To find the surface area of a sphere, substitute the radius into 4πr²; in the worked example r = 5 gives 4π(5)² = 100π. The sphere's surface area 100π is evaluated and written with a decimal comma as 314.2 cm². The surface area of the sphere is asked for correct to 1 decimal place.
